questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Both the location, language and culture

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy, we got a very informative presentation.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We got a lot information through the erasmus office

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I have heard other universities have a whole introduction week, maybe that is something you should consider, or atleast more than just an orientation event

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I used WG-gesucht, and there were alot of options, but i would also recommend living in a dorm, you just have to start applying pretty early. I can recommend STUWO

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Try to live close to a u-bahn og tram that goes to the uni, some of my friends lived more than 50 minutes away from campus, and they said it was the worst to spend so much time travelling each day

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Pretty easy, that had a huge catalogue of courses, and it was a bit confusing which one bachelor students and master students could choose between, and which courses from other faculties you were allowed to attend, but each time i was in doubt i just contacted my coordinator and they helped me.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You have to create an account through the university, and then on U:find/courses you can see all the courses and when the aplication period. Then you just press the link on U:find and it takes you to the regristration website. Its pretty easy

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The moobility coordinator

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Pretty succesful, unfortunately there were some courses, we i didnt get a spot because only 25 students could be in that course

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Choose courses that you find interesting, and choose a lot. You can always deregister from the courses. Also read what kind of exam it is, there were many different and very difficult options. But also some easy ones

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was very big and a lot of courses which i would never be able to take in Copenhagen

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was definetly higher than in Copenhagen, and they expected more reading and harder exams. But every teacher i had were so nice and helpful, once they saw that i was Erasmus.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A lot of my courses were huge classes with 400 participants, which i wasnt used to from copenhagen, but a lot of it was the same.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.answer:

070064 VO Österreichische Geschichte II (von ca. 1815 bis zur Gegenwart) (5 ECTS

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend either the courses about childrens literature, they were so exciting and different from what i normally would learn. Then i would also recommend the lectures called einführung, where the teachers dont expect you to have any knowledge of the subject before

questions.answer: alot of fees for registration that i lived in the city

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Less expensive were the housing, i had a lot of stories from other that vienna was very expensive, but i lived in a huge apartment for a very reasonable price

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: didnt really use them

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were a lot of sports programme, both football, running and swimming

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Heard a lot of people enjoyed the running groups

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Basicly anything in Vienna, the city is very big and there are so many speciel and different things you can do. Also there are so many free events around the city, some concerts and museum that are free. If you enjoy hiking there are also alot options for that. If the weather is nice you can also fo for a swim at the donau

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Took a couple of weeks but it was pretty easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Not really, the local students i vienna were very focused on their studies, and didnt really want to spend much time socializing, but try to see if there are other erasmus people in your classes, they are usually much more fun.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The fact that many students in vienna, didnt really want to socialize after class

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The art, architecture and the music. Also the café culture. They enjoy sitting in small cafés and just drinking coffe and relaxing. It very cute, and you feel like a local if you go in there and sit.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Go be a part of the whatsapp group for exchange students, you will get a mail with the link, everybody in the group are in the same situation as you, and they are so much fun. 
2. Dont be afraid to explore the city alone. i really enjoyed going swimming or walking through the beautiful stress alone. 
3. Ask for help if you are in doubt. Everyone at the university were so helpful

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Dont buy the cooffe from the vending machine, there are ants in them

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The academic things i learned and all the people i got to know. I will never forgot the friends and the good times i had

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being alone in a new city

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Dont be scared, it was the best months of my life. And dont forget to have fun, you dont need to lock yourself inside your room to read all day, you also there to learn the culture and the people of a new city.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
